title: the DSG Deepearth areas 30-31

banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 30-31, R548: printed pp. 97-98 (pdf 98-99) - the FINAL TWO AREAS of the individual area key: Area 30 the Interplanar Whirlpool (the placid Area 17 river gathering speed to the shaft, its 2,000-foot plunge down the 100-foot-diameter shaft into the deep lake; the breakwater landing for hauling out boats, the wide trail becoming long switchback stairs cut the full shaft length to the bottom landing; the lake filling many adjoining caverns, some completely water-filled, most ceilinged 20 feet or more above the surface; the placid southern outflow river and the aggressive northern current to the whirlpool cavern; the depths rarely shallower than 100 feet and in places 1,000 feet down; the kuo-toa and aboleth watching for Plane of Water intruders without dwelling here; the roaming aquatic carnivores - giant catfish, gar, scrags, lampreys, merrow, sea snapping turtles, giant pike - infesting Area 31 by the wide river; the waterfall-side nymphs guarding the water's purity; the nereid watch over the whirlpool cavern with reinforcements three turns after discovery - water elementals, water weirds, tritons, vardigg, and marid, one or two types unless the incursion is major; the clean plentiful water and the scant troll-and-ogre treasure; and the elemental vortex itself - the Areas 29 and 21 analog, a water-breathing journey to the Plane of Water past guardians defeated or persuaded, the good-leaning tritons), and Area 31 Darksea (the displayed portion a small fraction of the unknown whole, its waters reaching a hundred miles or more south and east; the mild saltiness short of surface seawater; the ceilings rising 1,000 feet above the water or dropping below it to block whole sections; the rare sloping boat shores against the prevailing ceiling-plummeting cliffs; the shallow-only-near-shore depths falling hundreds of feet to the 2,000-foot bottom; the aboleth dominion - a dozen or more massive buoyant cities adrift in the black waters, their parties ever eager for slaves and sinister-ritual prey; the unique giants squid, water nagas, verme and morkoth beside the subterranean sharks, barracudas, rays, dragon turtles and sea snakes; the kuo-toa's losing war for control, their presence a thing of the past within a few centuries; the sunless aquatic fungi - mushroom-like floaters and depth-drifting mold clouds - feeding the fish, the subterranean perch, trout and salmon among them, prey to the swarming carnivores; and the capital city of aboleth culture, three times the size of the others and encircled by 36 towers instead of the usual six, grandiose in all ways).
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~12557-12709) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (capture idx 229 = the printed p. 98 window carrying the Area 30 tail and Area 31 in full, with the Area 30 head carried in the previous idx windows); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the 2,000-ft plunge, the 100-ft shaft, the 20-ft ceilings, the 100-ft shallow bound and 1,000-ft lake bottoms, the three-turn reinforcements, the hundred-mile reach, the 1,000-ft ceilings, the 2,000-ft deepest, the dozen-plus cities, and the capital at three-times size with 36 towers against the usual six; the only garbles settled cross-read (the djvu seerns and var-dig for the capture seems and vardigg). SEAMS: the R518 water travel (the river, the lake and the boat notes), the Monster Manual denizens (the kuo-toa, aboleth, scrags, merrow, nereid, tritons, marid, morkoth, naga, dragon turtle), the PHB water breathing, and the Area 21/29 vortex procedure. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND - the FINAL round of the pp. 75-98 individual area key (areas 1 through 31 all pinned, R527 through R548): the Deepearth child gap-flip question REOPENS after this land (the R527/R533-R547 precedent held it open until the setting landed in full - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the plunge feet, the shaft diameter, the ceiling minimum, the lake shallow and deep bounds, the reinforcement turns, the reach miles, the ceiling high bound, the deepest feet, the capital size multiplier, and the capital and usual tower counts. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas; no dice appear in this round. The water-travel/MM/PHB seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open this round; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnaqFallFt
consts.comment: the river plunges 2,000 feet straight down the shaft.

consts.name: dnaqShaftDiaFt
consts.comment: the shaft the water plunges down is 100 feet in diameter.

consts.name: dnaqCeilMinFt
consts.comment: in most areas the ceiling rises 20 feet or more from the surface of the lake.

consts.name: dnaqLakeShallowFt
consts.comment: the lake's depth varies from cavern to cavern, but it is rarely shallower than 100 feet.

consts.name: dnaqLakeDeepFt
consts.comment: in some places the lake bottom is 1,000 feet below the surface.

consts.name: dnaqReinforceTurns
consts.comment: the nereid reinforcements arrive three turns after the intrusion is discovered.

consts.name: dnaqReachMiles
consts.comment: it is safe to assume the Darksea's waters reach a hundred miles or more to the south and east of the displayed area.

consts.name: dnaqCeilHighFt
consts.comment: in many places the chamber ceiling rises far above the water level, occasionally by as much as 1,000 feet.

consts.name: dnaqDeepFt
consts.comment: the water is shallow only near the infrequent shorelines; elsewhere the bottom falls hundreds of feet, and at its deepest the Darksea bottom is 2,000 feet below the surface.

consts.name: dnaqCapitalSizeMult
consts.comment: the capital aboleth city is about three times the size of the others.

consts.name: dnaqCapitalTowers
consts.comment: the capital city is encircled by 36 towers.

consts.name: dnaqCityTowersUsual
consts.comment: the usual aboleth city has six towers; the capital has 36 instead.

bools.name: dnaqRiverPlunge
bools.comment: the placid river flowing from Area 17 gradually picks up speed until it reaches the shaft, where it plunges straight down, finally splashing into the deep subterranean lake that makes up Area 30.

bools.name: dnaqBreakwaterLanding
bools.comment: just before the water plunges over the fall it passes a sturdy breakwater and landing where travelers can remove boats from the water.

bools.name: dnaqSwitchbackStairs
bools.comment: a wide trail follows the river into the shaft, becoming a long series of wide stairs cut into the rock opposite the waterfall, switchbacking down the entire length of the shaft to a bottom landing adjacent to the lake.

bools.name: dnaqAdjoiningCaverns
bools.comment: the lake itself fills many adjoining caverns; some are completely filled, making boat travel impossible.

bools.name: dnaqTwoOutflows
bools.comment: a wide, placid river slowly makes its way out of the lake to the south, and a more aggressive current carries water into a large cavern to the north where the whirlpool is located.

bools.name: dnaqWatcherRaces
bools.comment: both the kuo-toa and the aboleth wander these caves though neither race maintains dwellings here; they are often on the watch for intruders from the Plane of Water, who gain access to the Prime Plane through the whirlpool.

bools.name: dnaqAquaticCarnivores
bools.comment: aquatic carnivores roam the deep waters using the wide river to Area 31 as a means of infesting that area: giant catfish, giant gar, scrags (marine trolls), lampreys, merrow (aquatic ogres), giant sea snapping turtles, and giant pike; the marine trolls and ogres lair in small side caverns while the others roam in search of prey.

bools.name: dnaqNymphGuardians
bools.comment: a small group of nymphs resides in these caverns, living in caves half-filled with water very close to the waterfall; they jealously guard against intrusion and strive constantly to keep the water pure.

bools.name: dnaqNereidWatch
bools.comment: the large cavern containing the interplanar whirlpool is claimed by a host of creatures from the Elemental Plane of Water; an assortment of nereid perpetually guards the approaches, some keeping intruders at bay while others hasten to their own plane for reinforcements.

bools.name: dnaqWaterRoster
bools.comment: the Plane of Water creatures who answer the nereids' calls include water elementals, water weirds, tritons, vardigg, and marid; unless the incursion is a major one, only one or two types respond at a given time.

bools.name: dnaqCleanWater
bools.comment: the water is clean and plentiful; the air does not circulate well, but few of the creatures here breathe it, so characters have no shortage.

bools.name: dnaqScantTreasure
bools.comment: the caves of the ogres and trolls contain limited amounts of treasure, but little else of value can be found here.

bools.name: dnaqWaterVortex
bools.comment: the whirlpool cavern is an elemental vortex like the mud and lava vortices in Areas 29 and 21; characters must be able to breathe water to survive a journey to the Plane of Water, and the guardians must be defeated or persuaded that the characters serve a cause they support - a few, such as the tritons, lean towards good alignment.

bools.name: dnaqVastUnknownSea
bools.comment: the portion of the Darksea shown on the map represents only a small fraction of the total area of this huge body of water; the exact extent is unknown.

bools.name: dnaqMildlySalty
bools.comment: the waters of the Darksea are mildly salty, but not as salty as seawater on the surface.

bools.name: dnaqBlockedSections
bools.comment: in other places the ceiling drops to the water level or below, blocking off huge sections of the sea to all but underwater travelers.

bools.name: dnaqMixedShore
bools.comment: small portions of the shoreline are smooth rock sloping gradually into the water where boats can be pulled ashore; most of the shore is vertical stone cliffs plummeting from the ceiling deep into the sea, escapable only by a vertical climb.

bools.name: dnaqAbolethDominion
bools.comment: the dominant denizens of the Darksea are the aboleth: a dozen or more of their massive buoyant cities drift slowly around the black waters, and aboleth parties commonly travel the sea, always eager for more slaves and more prey for their sinister rituals.

bools.name: dnaqUniqueSeaLife
bools.comment: the Area 30 travelers are encountered here, plus creatures unique to the Darksea: giant squid, water nagas, verme, and the hideously evil morkoth.

bools.name: dnaqOceanPredators
bools.comment: other aquatic denizens include subterranean varieties of ocean predators: sharks, barracudas, rays, and even dragon turtles and sea snakes.

bools.name: dnaqLosingKuoToanWar
bools.comment: small groups of kuo-toa are occasionally encountered, but the men-fish are engaged in a losing war with the aboleth for total control of the Darksea; within a few centuries the kuo-toan presence will be a thing of the past.

bools.name: dnaqAquaticFungi
bools.comment: kelp and plankton cannot grow without sunlight, but many varieties of aquatic fungi have developed: some float on the water looking much like mushrooms, smaller varieties resemble clouds of molds floating at all depths.

bools.name: dnaqFisheries
bools.comment: many fish thrive on the fungi - including some of the monsters - plus subterranean varieties of perch, trout and salmon, all falling prey to the thriving carnivores that swarm the Darksea.

bools.name: dnaqAbolethCapital
bools.comment: the aboleth cities float through the Darksea much like their city in the Great Lake of Deepearth (Area 17); one city is the center of aboleth culture, about three times the size of the others and in all ways more grandiose.

examples.note: the plunge: 2,000 feet down the 100-ft shaft.
the lake: 20-ft minimum airspace, rarely shallower than 100 feet, bottoms 1,000 feet down.
the nereid: reinforcements three turns after discovery.
the Darksea: a hundred miles or more, 1,000-ft airspace, the 2,000-ft depth.
the capital: three times the size, 36 towers instead of the usual six.
